figure.name: Vladimir Lenin
figure.era: Russian Revolution and early Soviet state (1900-1924)
figure.role: Revolutionary theorist and Bolshevik leader focused on party organization, state power, imperialism, and revolution.
figure.hook: Lenin = theory, organization, revolution, and state power.
whyHere: Lenin belongs here because the socialist road becomes a governing problem in 1917: organization, revolution, state power, civil conflict, and party authority move from theory into institutions.

He matters because debates about socialism and communism often pass through Leninism, but Leninism is a specific revolutionary and party-state road, not a synonym for every public program or every socialist idea.
figure.cleanIdea: Lenin's road asks how a revolutionary party can organize power, and what happens when that organization becomes the state.

hallCard.timelineMeaning: The Bolshevik victory turns revolutionary theory into a problem of state power, party authority, civil conflict, and institutions.

ideas.title: Vanguard Party
ideas.plainDefinition: A vanguard party is a revolutionary organization that claims it can organize and lead the working class toward political power.
ideas.context: In the Lenin path, the party is not just a campaign machine. It is the central tool for discipline, theory, strategy, and state power.
ideas.whyMatters: Vanguard party matters because it separates Lenin's revolutionary road from democratic reform roads and from broad public-service arguments.

ideas.title: Revolutionary Theory
ideas.plainDefinition: Revolutionary theory is a framework for explaining political conflict and guiding revolutionary organization and action.
ideas.context: In the Lenin path, theory is treated as a practical organizing question, not just a classroom subject.
ideas.whyMatters: Revolutionary theory matters because movements do not only react to events. They also interpret events through a strategy.

ideas.title: State Power
ideas.plainDefinition: State power is the organized ability to make law, administer institutions, collect resources, command force, punish, and define public order.
ideas.context: In the Lenin path, state power is where revolutionary promises become institutions and coercive authority.
ideas.whyMatters: State power matters because it keeps the study guide focused on what governments actually do, not just what movements say they want.
